_comment: Lightning 2.0 Phase 3 remediation. An adversarial audit of the two migrations applied earlier the same night found a blocker and two majors. 20260921025504 created public.cash_cluster_epoch, backfilled it once and declared in its own proof that every cash_games row has an open epoch row, and then nothing maintained it: the first Cluster created afterwards had no epoch row, and because the same file made lightning_pool_session and lightning_instance reference (cluster_id, cluster_epoch), its first Phase 4 or Phase 5 write would have raised 23503. public.fn_cash_cluster_epoch_follows_its_game is an AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE trigger on cash_games that writes the genesis row, ends the open epoch and opens the successor when cluster_epoch moves forward, refuses a backwards move, and keeps the open epoch's mode in step - so Phase 5 bumps one integer and the history is correct by construction. 20260921025523 said three readers ask which table stands for a game; the catalogue said six, and the three it missed all govern the seat change, so on a feeder-first Cluster the lobby said nobody was in the main game, the door refused the wrong thing, and the planner would have routed a player onto the front table out of must-move order. fn_cash_game_lobby, fn_cash_seat_change_request, fn_cash_seat_change_plan and the tick's break candidate now all ask fn_cash_cluster_front_table, which is itself re-cut as three coalesced index lookups: the first restores the index condition the single ORDER BY lost, no boolean is sorted so a NULL main_index cannot outrank the real Main 1, and a breaking table is preferred last. The two hot scans read it into a local rather than once per row. fn_cash_cluster_open_table counts LIVE tables, so an R3 reopen no longer names a Cluster's one table after one of its own parts. Two non-partial indexes give the new epoch foreign keys something to check against.
